visual.general_description: Grayscale schematic of a cell-membrane lipid bilayer with receptors and ion channels, a brain, a neuron and a zonisamide molecule, connected by labelled arrows.
visual.detailed_description: A horizontal lipid bilayer is labelled "Extracellular" above and "Intracellular" below at the left. At the left a seven-helix transmembrane receptor-like structure carries ovals labelled "DA" and two labelled "5-HT" on the extracellular side. A solid arrow labelled "Stimulate" points from the area of these ovals up and to the right to a grayscale brain, beside which the text "Mesolimbic pathway" is printed. A second solid arrow labelled "Excited" leads from the brain to a neuron drawing labelled "Neuron". In the middle a Y-shaped channel/receptor spans the membrane; below it an oval "Ca2+" is printed beside the text "Zonisamide inhibit". At the right a wider funnel-shaped channel spans the membrane with ovals marked "Na+" (a downward arrow runs from one "Na+" into the channel), another oval partly illegible, and "K+" ovals on the intracellular side, with a second text "Zonisamide inhibit" beneath. A dark oval labelled "Zonisamide" at the upper right is joined to the channel by double wavy lines labelled "Restrain", without a visible arrowhead. No panel letters, numeric values or axes are present.

evidence.quote:
Fig. 3
Zonisamide inhibits the sustained high-frequency repetitive firing of action potentials dependent on Na^(+) and reduces the opening of T-type calcium channels, leading to the release of DA (dopamine) and 5-HT (serotonin). This excites nerve cells and stimulates the mesolimbic pathway, inducing and exacerbating psychiatric symptoms such as hallucinations, delusions/agitation, etc.
